exposure: Quality and availability of drinking water (source, distance to source, contamination, payment obligation, method of delivery for services, water appearance, unavailability)
Hygiene practices (hand washing with soap or detergents)
outcome: Microbial and physicochemical water contamination levels
Prevalence of poor sanitation practices (open defecation)
cohort: The study included 784 participants (60.2% female) from 33 villages in rural South Kordofan, Sudan, who were convenient samples from targeted villages and attendants of mobile clinics.
finding: The study revealed inadequate water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services in rural South Kordofan, characterized by high microbial water contamination, poor sanitation practices, and a disconnect between expressed satisfaction and actual service quality, largely attributed to armed conflict.
